source_text:
1.11
Ταράξιππον Εἰς τοῦτό ποτε ἐλάσαι τρυφῆς Συβαρίτας λόγος ὡς παρὰ δεῖπνον εἰς τὸ
συμπόσιον τοὺς ἵππους εἰσάγειν. Τοὺς δ' ἀκούσαντας αὐλήματος ἀνίστασθαι ἐπὶ τὼ
πόδε καὶ τοῖς προσθίοις ὥσπερ χειρονομοῦντας ὀρχεῖσθαι. Ὑβρισθέντα δὲ αὐλητὴν
εἰς Κροτωνιάτας αὐτομολῆσαι προσφάτως ἱππομαχίᾳ νενικημένους· μέγιστα δὲ
ὠφελῆσαι τὸ κοινὸν ἐπαγγείλασθαι, παραδώσειν γὰρ πᾶν τὸ Συβαριτικὸν ἱππικὸν
αἰχμάλωτον· πιστεῦσαι τοὺς Κροτωνιάτας αὐτῷ καὶ ἐπιτρέψαι στρατηγεῖν. Τὸν δέ,
ἀθροίσαντα τοὺς τῆς πόλεως αὐλητάς, δεῖξαι τὸ μέλος, καὶ ὅτε καιρὸς ἦν,
παρεγγυῆσαι τὴν ἐπὶ τοὺς πολεμίους ἔξοδον. Ὡς δὲ οἱ Συβαρῖται ἐπῆλθον πανδημεὶ
πολύ τι φρυαττόμενοι τῇ τῆς ἵππου περιουσίᾳ, καὶ ἀνεμίγησαν ἀλλήλαις αἱ
φάλαγγες, ὑπὸ σημεῖον ἕν, ηὔλησαν οἱ πάντες· συνήθους δὲ ἤχου ἀκούσαντες οἱ
ἵπποι ὥσπερ οἴκοι ἐδεδιδάχατο, ἀποσεισάμενοι τοὺς ἀναβάτας, ὑπωρχοῦντο πάντες. Τότε οὖν οἱ ἱππόται ἑάλωσαν κείμενοι καὶ οἱ ἵπποι ἐλήφθησαν ὀρχούμενοι,
ἀναστησάντων αὐτοὺς συνήθων μελῶν. Εὔχονται δὲ καὶ ἄλλοι, μάχεσθαι μέλλοντες,
οὐ μὴν ἀλλὰ καὶ θύουσιν, ἐν ἀγῶνι καθεστηκότες, ταραξίππῳ Ποσειδῶνι. Καὶ ἡμεῖς
δὲ εὕρομεν φάρμακον εὐχῆς ὀξύτερον, κρεῖττον πάντων ὁπόσα ἂν ἔχοις, οὗπερ ἐπὶ
τέλει πενταγώνῳ ηʹ τὸ εἶδος ἐγγέγραπται, ᾧ σημεῖα ὑπέρκειται παρυπάτης μέσων,
ῥῶ καὶ σίγμα ὕπτιον. Εἰς πυουλκοὺς ἐμβάλλεται καὶ εἰς παράταξιν κούφοις ἀνδράσιν
δίδοται φέρειν, ὡς εὐκόλως ὑπὸ τῷ στίφει τῶν προμαχομένων ἑστάναι. Οἳ μὲν οὖν
ἐπάγουσιν ἀλκῇ καὶ τάχει καὶ σιδήρῳ τεθαρρηκότες· ἄν τε οὖν κατάφρακτοι οὗτοι
τύχωσιν, ἄν τε καὶ ἄλλως ἐσταλμένοι, ἐς τὸν αὐτὸν σπεύδουσι κίνδυνον. Γενομένης
γὰρ τῆς ἐς τοὺς πεζοὺς ἐμβολῆς, οἳ μὲν προτεταγμένοι φέρουσιν τὴν ἐπιδρομὴν τῷ
τῶν ἀσπίδων φράγματι, οἳ δὲ τοὺς πυουλκοὺς ἔχοντες ἐκθλίβουσι τὸ φάρμακον εἰς
τὰς τῶν ἵππων ἀναπνοάς· (δεινὸς δὲ ὁ χυλὸς καὶ ἀνδράσιν εἰς βλάβην). Ἐπειδὰν οὖν
οἱ ἵπποι δέξωνται τὴν ὀδμὴν τοῦ κακοῦ, μεμήνασι καὶ φριμάσσουσι καὶ διὰ σπουδῆς
ἀνίστανται, ὥσπερ τὴν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἀναπνοὴν πεφοβημένοι, καὶ ἀνασκιρτῶσιν
ὄρθιοι. Πίπτουσι δὲ οἱ ἀναβάται ἀπὸ τῶν ἵππων χαμαί, ἕτοιμοι πρὸς ζωγρίαν ἅμα καὶ
σφαγήν, τοῖς αὑτῶν θώραξιν εἰς τὸ μὴ διαφυγεῖν πεπεδημένοι, ἢ πατούμενοι, ἢ
παιόμενοι.
pass_a_gloss: Horse-frightener. The story: Sybarites once drove to this of luxury as at dinner to-lead the horses into the symposium. And they, having-heard an aulos-tune, stand-up on the two hind-feet and with the front as-if gesturing dance. An aulos-player having-been-insulted deserted to the Crotoniates, freshly beaten in a horse-fight; he promised to-benefit the common-thing greatest, for he would-hand-over the whole Sybarite horse-force captive; the Crotoniates trusted him and allowed him to-general. And he, having-gathered the city's aulos-players, showed the tune, and when it was time, passed-the-word for the sally upon the enemies. As the Sybarites came-on with-the-whole-people, quite snorting with the surplus of horse, and the phalanxes mixed with one another, under one signal all piped; and the horses, having-heard the accustomed sound as they had-been-taught at home, having-shaken-off the riders, all danced-under. Then then the horsemen were-caught lying and the horses were-taken dancing, accustomed tunes having-set-them-up. Others also pray, being-about to-fight, and indeed also sacrifice, having-stood in contest, to Taraxippos Poseidon. And we too found a drug quicker than prayer, better than all you might have, whose form at the end in pentagon 8 has-been-inscribed, to-which signs are-set-above of parhypate meson, rho and inverted sigma. It is-put into pus-extractors and in array is-given to light men to-carry, so-as easily to-stand under the press of the front-fighters. Those then come-on having-trusted in strength and speed and iron; whether then these happen to-be cataphracts, or also otherwise equipped, they hurry into the same danger. For when the charge into the infantry has-happened, the front-ranked bear the onset by the fence of the shields, and those holding the pus-extractors squeeze-out the drug into the horses' breaths (and the juice is terrible even to men toward harm). When then the horses receive the smell of the evil, they go-mad and snort and stand-up in haste, as-if having-feared the breath from the earth, and they leap upright. The riders fall from the horses to-the-ground, ready toward capture and slaughter together, fettered by their own breastplates against escaping, either being-trampled or being-struck.
pass_b_english: The horse-frightener. The story is that the Sybarites once drove luxury to this point: they would lead the horses into the symposium at dinner. The horses, having heard an aulos-tune, stand up on the two hind feet and dance with the front as if gesturing with the hands. An aulos-player who had been insulted deserted to the Crotoniates, freshly beaten in a horse-fight. He promised to benefit the common thing to the greatest degree, for he would hand over the whole Sybarite horse-force captive. The Crotoniates trusted him and allowed him to general. He gathered the city's aulos-players, showed the tune, and when it was time passed the word for the sally upon the enemies.

When the Sybarites came on with the whole people, snorting quite with the surplus of horse, and the phalanxes mixed with one another, under one signal all piped. The horses, having heard the accustomed sound as they had been taught at home, shook off the riders and all danced. Then the horsemen were caught lying, and the horses were taken dancing, the accustomed tunes having set them up.

Others also, being about to fight, pray — and they also sacrifice, having stood in contest — to Taraxippos Poseidon. We too found a drug quicker than prayer, better than all you might have, whose form has been inscribed at the end in pentagon 8, over which are set the signs of parhypate meson: rho and an inverted sigma. It is put into pus-extractors and in the array is given to light men to carry, so that they may stand easily under the press of the front-fighters.

Those then come on having trusted in strength and speed and iron. Whether they happen to be cataphracts, or equipped otherwise, they hurry into the same danger. For when the charge into the infantry has happened, the front-ranked bear the onset by the fence of the shields, and those holding the pus-extractors squeeze the drug into the horses' breaths (the juice is terrible even to men for harm). When the horses receive the smell of the evil they go mad and snort and stand up in haste, as if they had feared the breath from the earth, and they leap upright. The riders fall from the horses to the ground, ready for capture and for slaughter together, fettered by their own breastplates against escaping, either trampled or struck.

choices.why: The lock names Poseidon under the cult-title Taraxippos; it is not a generic 'horse-panic' and not a person separate from the god in this clause.
